about: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next EXL3 3.05bpw_h5_ng5 on one RTX 3090: experts in pinned RAM behind a GPU expert cache, n-gram table on NVMe (trellis-serve 61846cb)
setup: NEEDS: 1x RTX 3090 24 GB (the server takes the whole card: 21.2 GiB at ready, 23.2 GiB after load; the expert cache auto-sizes to free VRAM, so nothing else may use the GPU); 68 GB of free system RAM (measured: scheduler peak RSS 63.4 GB + launcher 2.0 + detokenizer 1.7 + tokenizer helper 0.75; of it, page-locked: 45.8 GB routed experts + 8 GB n-gram row cache + 1.18 GB token embedding); 85.14 GB for the weights on a LOCAL NVMe SSD (52.3 GB of shards are read once at load; the 32.6 GB n-gram table is random-read with O_DIRECT while serving, so no network or tmpfs filesystem). Text only (vision is a follow-up). Launch = trellis-serve cuda/scripts/serve_flashnext_3090.sh at 61846cb (INT043 freeze) plus --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder, which the measured runs did not have, and a bridge network with --shm-size 64g where the measured runs used --ipc=host --ulimit memlock=-1. First start JIT-compiles the n-gram NVMe extension (~1 min, nvcc is in the image). Measured on omarchy (PCIe 4.0 x16, 26.2 GB/s pinned host-to-device): prefill 4k 2,092 / 32k 2,848 tok/s, decode 63.7 @0 / 62.4 @32k tok/s, needle 196,376 tokens PASS; a rented 3090 with 14-16 GB/s host-to-device decoded 53.2 tok/s (V001b), so PCIe bandwidth matters. SGLANG_EXL3_NGRAM_TIER=pinned keeps the n-gram table in RAM instead (+24.6 GB RAM, no NVMe needed).
